input: # divergent.tsv — where this repo's two ports DISAGREE, executed by both.
#   input  TOML source. Escapes \n \r \t \\ are decoded, as in spec/.
#   ts,go  what each port produces: a JSON value, or ERROR:<code>, or
#          ERROR:<code>@<row>:<col> when the POSITION is the disagreement.
#   why    the audit item, and where the repair lives.
# NOT A FIXTURE. A fixture fails when behaviour REGRESSES. This fails BOTH
# ways: when a port is repaired to agree with the other, the row still
# claims they differ, so the suite goes red and names the row to delete. A
# divergence recorded as a passing test of current behaviour survives its
# own repair, with nothing red — which is how the 2026-08 audit found 29
# recorded claims contradicted by execution.
# MEASURED 2026-08-19 by tasks/ax-parity-probe.js and re-measured in each
# port. The probe could not run on this repo at all until that day: it
# assumed one Go plugin surface and this repo exports the other, so it
# failed to COMPILE and reported "COULD NOT RUN". These four rows are the
# first cross-runtime measurement this repo has ever had beyond its
# fixtures.
# --- Audit P5: Go advances the error column in BYTES ---------------------
# TypeScript reports the column in characters; Go adds one per extra byte,
# so a two-byte 'é' costs two columns and a four-byte emoji costs four. The
# gap widens with the byte length of what precedes the failure, which is
# why all four rows below differ by a different amount.
# Engine repair: tabnas/parser#124. These rows go red on adoption, which is
# the signal to delete them.
# NOTE THE DIRECTION. json5's position rows go the OTHER way — Go reporting
# LOWER, because TypeScript counts UTF-16 code units and an astral
# character advances its column by two. That one is argued and PERMANENT.
# Same symptom, opposite sign, opposite verdict.
["ab😀cd" 1]
